bug_semantics: An attacker who can add an account identity can POST an identity string containing HTML or JavaScript to /accounts/<account>/identities. The backend stores that identity string and the account-identities GET endpoint returns it. On the WebUI account page, load_identities handed the returned objects directly to jQuery DataTables as data and selected the identity and type properties as columns. DataTables treated those string values as cell HTML, so merely viewing the affected account page inserted the persisted identity into the DOM and executed attacker-controlled script in the viewer's WebUI origin.
flaw_origin: Commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 created the account-administration page and lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js. Its new load_identities function passed the server response directly to DataTable with `data: data` and `columns: [{'data': 'identity'}, {'data': 'type'}]`, without encoding the identity before the HTML sink. The same feature commit also added the UI's identity-creation helper, completing the store-and-render path. The pre-existing backend identity model/API stored and returned the supplied identity as data; the vulnerability began when this commit added the unsafe browser rendering, not when later code was moved or refactored.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object for 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 names Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch> as both author and committer and contains only the subject `[RUCIO-2849] RucioUI account admin pages`; it has no message body, Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailer, bot identity, or other commit-object AI attribution.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-8wpv-6x3f-3rm5 describes POST /proxy/accounts/pentest/identities with an identity such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>, persistence, and execution when /ui/account?account=pentest is viewed; it declares rucio-webui fixed in 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1. Vulnerable flow at the fix parent: lib/rucio/web/rest/flaskapi/v1/accounts.py parses the POST identity and calls add_account_identity, while its GET generator serializes every result of list_identities; lib/rucio/core/identity.py add_identity assigns the supplied string directly to models.Identity.identity. The WebUI client lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rucio.js requests /accounts/<account>/identities, and account.js load_identities sent the returned objects directly to DataTables. `git log -L :load_identities:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003^` traces the vulnerable `data: data` identity/type block to 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 (2017-11-06), where account.js was a new file; the only later change shown before the encoding fix changed an unrelated url_param error sink. `git show --format=raw 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78` gives sole parent 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e and the exact author/committer/message above. Direct parent-tree checks are negative: `git cat-file -e 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js` reports that the path does not exist, and `git grep -E 'load_identities|identities_table|DataTable.*identit|identity.*DataTable' 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e -- lib/rucio/web/ui` returns no match. This proves the immediate parent lacks both the new file and an equivalent account-identity DataTable sink. Release introduction: `git tag --contains 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 --sort=version:refname` begins at 1.13.3; tag 1.13.3 contains account.js load_identities and `data: data`, while tag 1.13.2 has no account.js and 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 is not its ancestor. Fix: direct master commit b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 (`fix(WebUI): fix XSS using DataTable`, first committed to master on 2026-02-25) replaces direct response rendering with sanitisedData, encoding identity/type via `$('<div>').text(String(value)).html()` and retaining raw values only under non-displayed $identity/$type keys for API operations. The same patch was applied to release lines as a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 (contained by tag 35.8.3), abf5e978ee3910590a23c6705e6a0105c0b847c7 (contained by 38.5.4), and 80b91dd0c6737b2ab9aed039470e8e81028def41 (contained by 39.3.1); 3b6cea7848eea31a6342190d1cdb680b8fcb1eb2 carries it on the 39.4 line. A six-tag `git grep` verifies account.js:136 is still `data: data` in 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0, whereas 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1 contain sanitisedData and feed that encoded array to DataTables, exactly matching all three advisory patch boundaries. Release references: https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/35.8.3, https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/38.5.4, and https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/39.3.1.
reasoning: The security property that fails is output encoding at a browser HTML sink. Arbitrary identity text is intentionally valid backend data, so persistence alone is not the BIC; the exploitable mechanism appears when the account page first renders that server-controlled identity through DataTables without encoding. Line history identifies 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 as the first writer of the exact vulnerable load_identities block. It is an ordinary one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, backport, merge, or squash aggregate, so there is no smaller reconstructable member commit to substitute and no squash decomposition to record. Its direct parent 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e lacks account.js and any equivalent account-identity DataTable sink, satisfying parent absence. Tag history brackets introduction between 1.13.2 and 1.13.3, and source checks across each advisory boundary show vulnerable direct rendering in the immediately preceding tags and encoded rendering in the three first-patched tags. The master fix b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 is the direct source patch; a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 is recorded as fix_sha because it is the patch carried by the advisory's first listed fixed release, with the other release-line copies fully identified in evidence. Finally, AI attribution is judged only from the BIC object: it has a named non-bot author/committer and no AI trailer or marker. Later fix authorship and commit messages do not affect attribution. The closed result is therefore NOT_AI.
